chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) one day, and he had entered Al-Masjid Al-Haram for the Asr prayer. When he was before the rows (of worshippers) and they bowed, he bowed. Then he prostrated the two prostrations, then he stood up and continued until he joined the rows.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Sadiq do when he entered the mosque after the congregation had already bowed?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility in congregational prayer etiquette, specifically the permissibility of an individual completing their own rak'ahs before joining the Imam or congregation. It underscores the scholarly principle that missing the initial takbir or joining late does not invalidate the prayer, provided the essential pillars are fulfilled, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt.
